description: Containers fail to launch after restarting the Mesos agent. The executor logs show a 'connection refused' error when contacting the Docker daemon socket.
comments: Reproduced on 3 agents after a rolling restart. Looks like the daemon socket is stale until Docker itself is restarted.
resolution: Restarting the Docker daemon after the agent restart resolved the stale socket issue. Added a note to the runbook to restart Docker before Mesos agent on maintenance windows.

summary: Agent fails to re-register after network partition
description: When a network partition heals, the agent does not automatically re-register with the master and remains marked as unreachable.
comments: Master logs show the agent's re-registration timeout expiring before the partition healed. Increasing the timeout was suggested.

summary: Persistent volume not reattached after agent restart
description: After restarting an agent that hosts persistent volumes, tasks fail to reattach to their existing persistent volume and instead attempt to create a new one.
comments: Confirmed this only happens when the agent work_dir is on a different mount than expected. Checked disk profile module for related issues.
resolution: Fixed by ensuring the agent is restarted with the same --work_dir flag used originally, and by pinning the disk profile module version. Documented in the persistent volumes runbook.

summary: Framework fails to receive offers after scale-down
description: After scaling down the cluster, one framework stops receiving resource offers even though resources are available.

summary: Improve logging for executor registration timeouts
description: Executor registration timeouts are logged with insufficient context, making it hard to tell which agent or task caused the timeout.
comments: Agreed this is a quick win. Added agent_id and task_id to the log line.
resolution: Added agent_id, task_id, and elapsed_ms fields to the executor registration timeout log message.

summary: Docker containers leak file descriptors under high task churn
description: Under high task churn (many short-lived tasks), the Docker daemon on the agent host accumulates open file descriptors until it hits the OS limit and stops accepting new containers.
comments: Tracked down to log driver not closing streams cleanly on fast container exit. Similar to a known upstream Docker issue.
resolution: Upgraded the Docker daemon version and set an explicit ulimit for the mesos-agent systemd unit. No recurrence after two weeks of monitoring.

summary: Master crashes on malformed framework re-registration message
description: Sending a malformed re-registration message from a custom framework causes the master process to crash instead of rejecting the message.
comments: Crash confirmed via core dump analysis. Root cause is missing validation on the FrameworkInfo protobuf before processing.
resolution: Added strict validation of FrameworkInfo fields on re-registration; malformed messages are now rejected with an error response instead of crashing the master.

summary: Add support for cgroups v2 resource isolation
description: Requesting support for cgroups v2 so agents can run on newer Linux kernels/distros that have dropped cgroups v1.
comments: Significant effort; will require changes to the isolator module. Tracked as a multi-release effort.

summary: Disk usage metrics incorrect for overlay filesystem
description: Disk usage reported for tasks using the overlay filesystem driver is consistently lower than actual usage, causing disk quota checks to pass when they should fail.
comments: Root cause: disk usage collector was only summing the upper directory, not accounting for merged layers.
resolution: Updated the disk usage collector to account for the full overlay merged directory size. Verified against manual du measurements.

summary: VPN-based agent registration fails after credential rotation
description: Agents connecting to the master over a VPN fail to re-register after the corporate VPN credentials are rotated, even though the underlying network path is otherwise healthy.
comments: Similar symptom to MESOS-1002 but root cause is different -- this is a credential/auth issue, not a partition/timeout issue.
resolution: Documented the credential rotation procedure to include restarting the mesos-agent process so it re-authenticates against the VPN concentrator using the new credentials.
